turn_text: Senator Cassidy, thank you so much for your time. And here's the market minute with Plats Senior Editor, Jordan Bloom.

India only produces less than 1% of the world's oil supplies, but the South Asian nation sure did make it a tougher week for oil bulls on the markets. India is, after all, the third largest consumer of oil, and it is tragically now reporting close to 300,000 new COVID cases per day. Those are pretty astounding numbers, no matter how large the total population. Then there's Japan, the fourth largest consumer of oil, fighting a COVID surge and declaring targeted states of emergency. And Brazil, another top 10 consumer, continues to be embroiled in the worst of the pandemic. So as the US and Europe continue to show signs of life with the ongoing vaccine rollout, much of the rest of the world looks murkier without as much access to vaccines. We saw crude prices plunge Tuesday and Wednesday before seeing smaller upticks on Thursday and Friday as markets weighed rising gasoline demand and economic data in much of the Western Hemisphere. But a ceiling is still expected to remain on crude prices until the Asian COVID spike shows signs of slowing. That's why there is renewed interest this week in OPEC plus meetings to see if they will consider backing off any of their plans to further unwind production cuts in May, June and July. This was Jordan Bloom with your Market Minute.
